manifest.reason: Keep the draw loop as it is: pose(), render(), the stencil guard passes, translucent twins, the look-through image, shadows and fitting are the runtime the owner judged. Rewrite the GLB front end (create/configure). Today it: (1) can only open models through the catalog; (2) has no Draco/meshopt/KTX2 decoders; (3) resolves external URIs against the wrong base; (4) parses the GLB before any WebGLRenderer exists, which KTX2 needs; (5) aborts the whole load on any subsystem throw; (6) does no units, origin, orientation, transform, triangle or texture checks and writes no report; (7) relies on optical-material's camelCase-partRole-or-transmission rule for lens and crystal identity. In the rewrite: drop the canonical-lens branches; parse with all three decoders and a base path taken from the model URL; check §2 (bounds, units, orientation, baked transforms, finite triangles, lens material found) and return a report; turn every non-§2 failure into a warning plus fallback (each subsystem in its own try block); expose a capture accessor (scene, camera, lens meshes, eyewear pose, part-class masks) in place of the private fields the prototype reads.

I agree with the rewrite and with removing the canonical caster, effective groups, the float peel and the overflow rethrow. But the stash caster change is not self-contained. It is the shadow half of the stash temple-clip.ts change, so take both or neither. The shadow clip receives the visible clip's configuration and exists to match the drawn shafts. Stash temple-clip leaves front-profiled parts unclipped and clips profiled temples by their declared side, not sign(x). Stash shadow with 75 temple-clip breaks in two ways. A front-profiled part that reaches behind the cutoff is discarded on screen but still casts a detached cheek shadow. A profiled temple part that crosses x=0 is clipped by one side on screen and the other in the shadow. Rule: take the stash version only together with stash temple-clip.ts and part-visibility.ts (untracked). If the temple reviewer keeps 75 temple-clip, take 75 here. Also, partVisibilityOf throws on a malformed value inside the constructor's try, which disposes and rethrows. In 75's create() that aborts the whole load, so arview must turn it into a warning plus the legacy path.

The core of crystal transparency. It is an opaque twin that mixes in the camera or look-through image through the material's volume and (1 - F), with clearcoat and the crystal reflection limit. Its one throw requires the material to be classified as translucent frame, so crystal works only if lens identification classifies it as frame (arview's partRole / part_role / name-token order fixes TF r9).

Keep the class, but delete the readMaterialLensAppearance clause now rather than 'only if lens-appearance.ts is dropped'. Once lens-material.ts is dropped, no material is ever converted to a canonical lens. A lens from a retired-route GLB that still carries the descriptor then draws through its native fallback, and that fallback always transmits. Line :39 still says this lens is 'not legacy optics'. The renderer then passes internalTransmissionIsLensInput=false, so temple visibility stops excluding the arms from Three's transmission pre-pass, and the far arm shows through the near lens. The first reviewer's lens-material.ts claim that such a GLB 'renders through its glTF fallback with a warning' is therefore true only after this edit. The better fix is for the renderer rewrite to strip userData.gltfExtensions.LENSES_lens_appearance at load, with a report warning. Every other kept reader would then see a plain native material: optical-material.ts throws on a malformed descriptor, and studio/viewer.ts refuses the file.

Converts KHR_materials_volume attenuation from metres to centimetres; without it, translucent fronts and volume lenses render black. Also the shared Beer-Lambert term for shadows and twins. The owner-judged visual fit, and the reveal gate. Two notes for arview: the AR size is not the GLB's metric size (auto scale times a 1.08 preference), and captures must let the fit settle frontally first or use a fixed-scale mode. It never inspects the GLB.

Not a plain keep. First, :9 imports GLASSES_METERS_TO_CENTIMETERS from catalog.ts, which the plan drops, so the file as listed breaks the build. Second, :46 hard-codes 'mesh-local metres times 100' into protectionProjection, which the renderer also calls directly for fitting. If arview applied its mm/cm fallback as a node or asset scale, every protection rectangle would project about 1000x too large for a mm file. projectBounds would then hit the near plane, createProtection would return null on every frame, and hair would be withheld silently (safeFallback). The fit projection would be equally wrong. So arview must BAKE the unit conversion into vertex positions, and scale thickness and attenuationDistance to match. Never use a node scale. The same metre assumption sits in the renderer's ×100 sites, the shadow and clip shaders (mesh-local xz), ARM_LATERAL_MIN_M and AUTHORED_FRAME_FRONT_MIN_Z_M. Edit: import the constant from a units module, and document the baked-metres precondition or take the asset scale as a parameter.

The area notes say drop this test, but only one of its three tests is canonical. The first two cover the native transmissive-lens lensenv path (renderer.ts:532-538): the lens owns the scene-room environment map at 0.8 × lensenv, and without lensenv it is left to scene.environment. That path is fed by the ?lensenv= model handover that WP1.5's webcam page ports, and every Studio GLB uses native lenses, so its only coverage must stay. Drop the canonical test and its descriptor fixture. Replace the catalog fixture with the direct model definition.

Repoint the catalog and lens-appearance imports.

I agree with the verdict and the source. I disagree with four parts of the reason. (1) The r9 prediction is right, but its premise is wrong. external.ts:11/:62 applies -0.11 only when ?clip is absent. The Studio always sends ?clip: -0.14 for legacy assets, max(-0.14, arm tip + 1e-6) for profiled ones, and -0.14 on failure. r9 still refuses at 75:151 (startZM -0.1622 <= -0.14). The plan's ':194 refuses crystal temples' cannot happen for r9 in either copy, even with a deeper clip: r9's opaque 'Embedded core' hardware is an eligible posterior opaque shaft. (2) Stash :137 does not fix crystal. A KHR transmission material loads with transparent=false, so 75's '!material.transparent' already let crystal through, and :137 only fixes alpha-BLEND arms. Crystal arms fail only when lens classification marks them optical. The lever is lens identification. In the plan's order, step 3 must be an asset-level last resort, used only when steps 1-2 find no lens, and legacy part_role frame/temple_*/hardware must count as an explicit non-lens signal. Otherwise r9's 'Crystal acetate' (transmission 1) becomes lens again at step 3 and :151 comes back. (3) The proposed fallback 'accept partRole + side' is unsafe as written. partRole 'frame' alone must not mark a part as fixed front: older 'frame' tags cover whole frames including the arms, and that would freeze the arms and give zero eligible vertices. Keep the stash geometric test, isAuthoredFrontFrame (all vertices z >= -0.03, identity transform chain). Take sides from the x sign, never from names: r9's legacy 'temple_left' is at +x, while FT1119/Prada region temple_left is at -x. (4) Units. The identity check at 75:143-145 is relative to root, and every threshold reads raw mesh-local positions. A millimetre file normalised by scaling the root or the asset group therefore passes :144-145 and runs every metre threshold on millimetre numbers without any error. Normalisation must rewrite the vertex buffers (and the KHR volume distances, which renderer.ts:459 assumes are metres). Also: converting only validatePartVisibility's throws to warnings is not enough. The first refusal happens in classification, before rear-drop, and partVisibilityOf throws on every call, so after warning it must return null.

I agree with the verdict and the source. Three corrections and one omission. (1) Build break the review misses: continuity imports protection.ts, and protection.ts imports GLASSES_METERS_TO_CENTIMETERS from eyewear/catalog.ts. 'No file in this set imports a module expected to be dropped' is therefore false transitively. Deleting catalog code breaks continuity, renderer.ts and external.ts unless GLASSES_METERS_TO_CENTIMETERS, GLASSES_OFFSET_CM, EyewearDefinition, eyewearById and registerModelingAutoEyewear move to a kept module first. (2) 'One registration pins every later model.glb' is overstated for the current code. installExternalModel runs once per page for the single ?model=, so a collision needs a page that loads several handed-over models, such as an arview capture batch reusing one page. The Studio always sends ?sha256, so continuity was on for every Studio handover. The real reason to drop the pin is unchanged: the renderer hashes the same bytes it parses. (3) 'crystal or BLEND arms missing' at 75:97 is wrong for crystal: transmission does not set transparent, so crystal arms drop out only when classified as lens. (4) Omission: lensRearZM (75:98 / stash :98) takes the minimum over every lens-classified vertex. r9 under the 75/main classification gives startZM = -0.1622 <= cutoff, so 'span missing' fires and the endpoint tracker turns off without any message. Compute the lens rear only from lens geometry forward of -0.03 m and warn, as for rear-drop.

I agree with keep and with taking the stash. The review misses one dependency that matters. The stash skips front-region meshes per mesh (stash :30), but it wraps per material (owned.has at :33), and profiled arms get no z gate (:56). If a material instance is shared by a front part and an arm, the arm wraps it, and the front then blends toward the camera wherever the hair mask is set. Side hair erases the frame front, which is the exact failure the stash comment says it prevents. This is safe only together with the stash optical-material.ts classification, which gives front and temple_left/temple_right separate material instances. The real assets share materials: Prada's 'Milk ivory' is on the front and both temples, and FT1119's 'Champagne alloy' is on the eyewire (front) and the T arms (temple). The untracked test proves the order: classifyAssetMaterials, then createHairOcclusion, then an assert that the front has no hair shader. Any region resolver that infers regions without LENSES_part_visibility must give the same per-region material split. Citation fix: 'skips only isOpticalMaterial' is 75:27, not 75:33. Units: the shader reads raw position.xz (stash :43), so millimetre models must be rescaled in the vertex buffers, not through a node scale.

Builds the observed lower-face polygon used for cheek occlusion from the canonical face topology and live landmarks. No GLB input and no throws: the constructor swallows boundary errors and evaluate() returns null on bad input. Identical in 75, stash and main.

A fragment-shader truncation plus camera blend at the temple end; it never changes geometry. All throws are configuration or API checks, not model acceptance. validateTempleClip (75:26-36) checks values the renderer computes itself (stash renderer.ts:335-341). The disposed checks are at 75:119/:134. prepareRender (75:141/:144) needs an sRGB CanvasTexture or render-target camera source with integer render size, so arview's capture harness must supply one even on plain backgrounds. Also imported by eyewear-shadow.ts:8-9, and rear-drop.ts uses TEMPLE_BLEND_LENGTH_LOCAL_M from it.

Filters the observed face shape for the private cheek-depth pass. No GLB input and no throws: failures reset history and return false. 75 = stash; the only difference from main is line endings (diff --strip-trailing-cr is empty).

The hair-first endpoint tracker over continuity paths; identical in 75, stash and main. Its only throw (75:47-49) cannot be reached from a model. The renderer derives maximumZM = max(cutoff, min(-.055, cutoff + .025, startZM - .008)) (stash renderer.ts:329-332), and continuity already requires startZM > cutoff (75 continuity.ts:103). It is built only when a continuity model exists (stash renderer.ts:812-813), so it depends on the continuity rewrite making continuity available for handed-over models. Without a hair mask (synthetic captures) it stays in the fixed-cap 'fallback' state.

Head-local lateral fit of the occluder from canonical face landmarks; it changes the occluder, never the eyewear. Its only throw (75:15-16) is the ratio range against WIDTH_FIT constants. No GLB input. 75 = stash; the only difference from main is line endings.

Builds the closed posterior head depth volume from canonical-face.json (read through publicDir from ar/public) plus the TEMPLE_HEAD_VOLUME ellipsoid. Every throw (75:13, :16, :24, :27, :37, :45, :57) checks the fixed canonical-face topology, never the GLB. It supplies canonicalFaceOuterBoundary to temple-cheek-contact.ts. 75 = stash; the only difference from main is line endings.

Blends fitted canonical temple-side face samples into the observed face, in the eyewear's pose. Its throws (75:24, :27) are per-frame input checks on values the renderer supplies. No GLB input. 75 = stash; the only difference from main is line endings.

I agree with keep and with taking the stash. The evidence needs three corrections. (1) The '75' line numbers are stash line numbers. In 75 the side-without-samples return is :90 (not :93), and the evaluator nulls are :99, :105 and :106 (not :102, :108, :109). (2) The crystal claims are wrong. 75:72 skips material.transparent, which is alpha-BLEND only. Crystal (KHR transmission) arms already produced samples in 75 unless lens classification made them optical. The stash :75 change helps alpha-BLEND arms, not crystal. (3) 'Already the warning-plus-fallback pattern arview wants' is only half true: the null is silent. counts[side] === 0 (stash :93) means one arm never reaches the terminal band, i.e. a missing or stub arm, which is a real geometry error. The renderer only keeps the cap or sets fitLimited, and no reason reaches any report. arview must report it, from rear-drop's per-side arm inventory or from a reason this evaluator returns. A declared side on the wrong half of X (temple_left at +x) also nulls the fit silently through the side sign at stash :99/:109. The region resolver must therefore check declared sides against the x sign.

I agree with rewrite and with taking the stash, plus two points the review misses. (1) frontZM is the minimum z over every lens-classified vertex (75:140-148 / stash :141-149). Under the 75/main classification r9's crystal counts as lens, so frontZM is about -0.1472. That does not throw, but the legacy gates (z < templeFrontalFront at stash :278/:287, z >= templeVisibilityFront at :354) then exclude almost every arm fragment, and the near-arm overlay and cheek occlusion turn off with no message. frontZM must come only from lens geometry forward of -0.03 m, with a warning, as for rear-drop. (2) The overlay 'defect' is real only for alpha-BLEND arms, and the hiding is deliberate. wrap() forces the clone to transparent=false and depthWrite=false (stash :338), so just removing the transparent check at :328 would draw an alpha-BLEND arm opaque in front of the head. A fix needs a blended overlay (blending kept, coverage multiplied into alpha). Crystal (KHR transmission) arms are unaffected: they load with transparent=false and already get transmissive overlays (stash :332-337). Also, the stash optical-material per-region material split is required here for the same reason as in hair-occlusion. wrapFrontal is per material, and profiled arms have no x/z gate, so a front sharing an arm's material would get arm cheek-occlusion.

Keep the ?model= handover (parse, then install), but replace the silent range fallbacks with reported warnings. Clip, width and digest should come from the model's own bytes and geometry; URL values become overrides or cross-checks. The current defaults reproduce a defect this code documents itself, and a stale digest refuses the whole model.

The verdict is correct and the reason needs one fix. As written, 'make the register refusals warnings' is unsafe for the clip. The -0.2..-0.03 m range at catalog.ts:94 is the precondition of three render refusals. A warned but unclamped clip would therefore move the refusal into configure() and refuse the whole model. The rewrite has to warn and then clamp into [-0.2, -0.045]. The same applies to external.ts's proposed 'derive the clip from the rearmost temple geometry'. That derivation also has to run after millimetre detection: a millimetre-scaled GLB puts the arm end near z ≈ -140 units, and the result must be rescaled or fall back with a loud warning. Clamping a millimetre value would silently produce -0.2.

This is the lens/frame classifier every renderer pass relies on. Start from the stash version, because the stash render edits need it. Then replace its identification. Today it reads only camelCase node/mesh partRole == 'lens', with an unwarned transmission>0 fallback. arview needs: (1) partRole on node, mesh or material, plus legacy part_role starting with 'lens'; (2) whole-word name tokens; (3) transmission or alpha<1 only with a warning. Each decision is recorded for report.json.

This is the canonical LENSES_lens_appearance response math that five render modules import. Native Studio GLBs do not use it, and its refusals can be handled at classification without editing this file.

The verdict says 'keep', but the stated plan changes the code. It turns six throws into warnings, swaps the camelCase-only role reader for the shared legacy-aware reader, and replaces the 1e-12 transform epsilon. Under 'keep' it would be copied verbatim and every throw would stay. partVisibilityOf throws on a malformed profile, and it is called on every render path. So the warning-plus-fallback has to live inside this module: return null plus a recorded warning. Callers cannot each be expected to catch it. Take the stash^3 file as the base.

files.reason: Keep the draw loop as it is: pose(), render(), the stencil guard passes, translucent twins, the look-through image, shadows and fitting are the runtime the owner judged. Rewrite the GLB front end (create/configure). Today it: (1) can only open models through the catalog; (2) has no Draco/meshopt/KTX2 decoders; (3) resolves external URIs against the wrong base; (4) parses the GLB before any WebGLRenderer exists, which KTX2 needs; (5) aborts the whole load on any subsystem throw; (6) does no units, origin, orientation, transform, triangle or texture checks and writes no report; (7) relies on optical-material's camelCase-partRole-or-transmission rule for lens and crystal identity. In the rewrite: drop the canonical-lens branches; parse with all three decoders and a base path taken from the model URL; check §2 (bounds, units, orientation, baked transforms, finite triangles, lens material found) and return a report; turn every non-§2 failure into a warning plus fallback (each subsystem in its own try block); expose a capture accessor (scene, camera, lens meshes, eyewear pose, part-class masks) in place of the private fields the prototype reads.
evidence: src/render/renderer.ts:16-71 (75): GLTFLoader (:23) is the only loader imported, with no DRACOLoader, KTX2Loader or MeshoptDecoder. three 0.185.1 GLTFLoader.js:520-521 + :1916-1918 throws 'No DRACOLoader instance provided.' whenever KHR_draco_mesh_compression is listed in extensionsUsed. Meshopt (:1619-1621) and KTX2 (:1476-1478) throw only when listed in extensionsRequired; otherwise they fall back silently.

corrections.reason: Not a plain keep. First, :9 imports GLASSES_METERS_TO_CENTIMETERS from catalog.ts, which the plan drops, so the file as listed breaks the build. Second, :46 hard-codes 'mesh-local metres times 100' into protectionProjection, which the renderer also calls directly for fitting. If arview applied its mm/cm fallback as a node or asset scale, every protection rectangle would project about 1000x too large for a mm file. projectBounds would then hit the near plane, createProtection would return null on every frame, and hair would be withheld silently (safeFallback). The fit projection would be equally wrong. So arview must BAKE the unit conversion into vertex positions, and scale thickness and attenuationDistance to match. Never use a node scale. The same metre assumption sits in the renderer's ×100 sites, the shadow and clip shaders (mesh-local xz), ARM_LATERAL_MIN_M and AUTHORED_FRAME_FRONT_MIN_Z_M. Edit: import the constant from a units module, and document the baked-metres precondition or take the asset scale as a parameter.

VERDICT: arview's non-render core (pipeline, face, camera, hair, audit) ports unchanged. Six areas need work:
- rewrite optical-material, external, catalog, main.ts, vite.config and prepare-assets;
- drop all of src/studio/*, studio-viewer.html, publish-site and prepare-hair-assets.

The biggest finding is the crystal r9 refusal. It is a lens-identification bug, not a crystal-geometry problem:
- r9 tags its parts with legacy snake_case `part_role` (frame, hardware, lens_left, lens_right, temple_left, temple_right).
- The 75 and stash code read only camelCase `partRole` (75 optical-material.ts:39-46; stash part-visibility.ts:17).
- So every r9 material counts as untagged. 'Crystal acetate' has transmissionFactor 1 and is shared by the front and both temples, so the transmission rule (75:124-128) makes the frame and temples OPTICAL.
- rear-drop then finds no opaque posterior shaft.

DIFF FACTS (verified with diff and git diff, read-only):
- In this scope, 75 and stash differ only in README.md, src/main.ts (one display fix, :355-356) and src/eyewear/optical-material.ts. The untracked addition is src/eyewear/part-visibility.ts.
- main..75ae133 in this scope changes config.ts, main.ts, optical-material.ts, vite.config.ts and README.md, and adds studio/* plus studio-viewer.html.
- The cmp differences against main's working tree for pipeline.ts, lens-appearance.ts, index.html and style.css are line endings only; git diff is empty.
- ar/public (38 MB) is identical in main, 75 and stash, so publicDir='../../ar/public' serves the exact runtime assets.

COUPLING:
- Taking ANY stash render edit (rear-drop, continuity, temple-*, hair-occlusion, eyewear-shadow) forces the stash optical-material.ts and part-visibility.ts. Stash temple-visibility.ts:8,155 imports isAuthoredFrontFrame, and six stash render files import part-visibility.ts.
- Dropping studio needs render-scope edits: renderer.ts:25-26, 84-85, 199, 293-316, 418, 432, 960; live-renderer.ts:14, 65-66. Also config.ts:77 and vite.config.ts:13.
- Test fallout: drop tests/studio-materials.test.ts and qa/studio-preview-smoke.*; rewrite tests/external-eyewear.test.ts.

CATALOG cannot simply be deleted. renderer.ts, protection.ts, live-renderer.ts, audit/reference.ts:73, external.ts, main.ts and the prototype page.js:4,38 import EyewearDefinition, GLASSES_METERS_TO_CENTIMETERS, GLASSES_OFFSET_CM, DEFAULT_EYEWEAR_ID, eyewearById, isEyewearId and registerModelingAutoEyewear. Shrink it to those plus a local-model slot.

?MODEL HANDOVER (external.ts:35-50):
- clip, width and lensenv fall back silently when out of range.
- The default clip of -0.11 reproduces the 'arm ends ~4 cm short' defect documented at catalog.ts:21-24.
- width is cosmetic: fit width comes from the lens bounds (renderer.ts:486-488).
- A stale sha256 refuses the whole model (renderer.ts:415, then continuity.ts:47).
- Pins are keyed by filename, and every Studio delivery is named model.glb (continuity.ts:21-32).
- arview should derive clip and width from the GLB, hash the bytes itself, and turn every fallback into a report warning. The width check is also how WP1.2's millimetre-scaled files get detected.

LENS ID ORDER, to implement in the rewritten optical-material.ts and record per material in report.json:

read.area_notes:
Verdict: of 82 qa files (59 in 75 = stash tracked, plus 23 untracked), 4 keep as-is, 17 rewrite, 61 drop.
- Keep as-is: the face-a fixture, its .gitignore, the portrait contract, the contract test.
- Rewrite: 17 files. Two are near-keeps that only need a small edit: provider-comparison-lighting.mjs is kept with an optional rename, and geometry-comparison.mjs needs only one change (external resources become a warning).

The 4 kinds of drop:
1. All optical-group and canonical-lens research.
2. The live-site page gates tied to the shipped catalog: fit/pipeline/shadow smokes, shadow-stability, measure, camera probes.
3. The publish verifier.
4. The product-specific native-crystal probe.

Every 75 qa file except the 10 that 75ae133 added or changed is byte-identical (CRLF aside) to main's ar/qa, so drops lose nothing: they stay runnable from ar/. The 10 are portrait-preview x4, provider-comparison.mjs, -ar.html, -lighting.mjs, -lighting.test.mjs, and studio-preview-smoke x2.

The stash changes only 4 qa files: portrait-preview.html, provider-comparison-ar.html, provider-comparison.mjs and provider-comparison-lighting.test.mjs. All 4 changes are temple-cutoff wiring.

"Provider harness = drop?": only the raw stage (provider-comparison.html) is a provider harness. The -ar stage (provider-comparison.mjs --stage=ar + provider-comparison-ar.html) is how the Studio captured AR views: source-before blender_agent/preview.py:121,188 -> bsa/archeck.run, and archeck.py:4 says it 'runs ar/qa/provider-comparison.mjs --stage=ar'. That is the runtime the owner judged on, and the prototype page.js copies its detection(). Rewrite it into 'arview capture', with the page.js variants and junction crops added.

Survivors by role:
- capture runner/page (provider-comparison.mjs/-ar.html + lighting module);
- worn portrait (portrait-preview.{mjs,html} + contract);
- webcam page + synthetic-webcam proof (astra-preview + astra-preview-smoke);
- native render tool for compare_to_photos and relief views (geometry-comparison family; the Studio called it from geometry_comparison.py:178);
- synthetic crystal loader smoke (studio-preview-smoke);
- deep-front negative control (part-visibility-probe);
- geometry temple clip (temple-cutoff, rewritten).

Cross-cutting fixes for the rewrites:
(a) Every harness builds Vite with configFile:false, so arview's vite.config publicDir (../../ar/public) never applies. Each must pass publicDir explicitly (best through one shared helper). Affected: 75 portrait-preview.mjs:54, provider-comparison.mjs:70, studio-preview-smoke.mjs:45, untracked part-visibility-probe.mjs:108. Pages fetch /models/canonical-face.json, and the renderer loads the face task, hair tflite and mediapipe wasm from public.
(b) Every page registers through catalog.ts registerModelingAutoEyewear, which requires templeClipLocalZM in -0.2..-0.03 (catalog.ts:94) and width 60-250 (:93), mostly with a fixed -.14. Switch to arview's registration API (external.ts installExternalModel also goes through catalog), with a geometry-derived clip and a warning fallback.
(c) Snapshot lists that hard-code public/models/* or catalog.ts under root will throw in arview (portrait-preview.mjs:32-36, native-crystal-probe.mjs:27). Compute import closures over src/ and qa/ instead.
(d) The hard throws in the pages (pose rejected, fit not settled, continuity failure, safeFallback) must become report warnings. A REAL geometry error, such as one temple side with no geometry (temple-cutoff.mjs:38-40), must be flagged in report.json, not hidden by the fallback.

Breakage outside qa/ to fix when porting:
- 75 tests/provider-harness-sources.test.ts:15,39-54 pins exact strings of provider-comparison.mjs/-ar.html (including the catalog.ts closure root): rewrite it with the capture runner.
- 75 tests/config.test.ts:124 reads qa/measure.mjs: drop that assertion, or keep measure.mjs.
- 75 package.json:14 'test:qa' globs qa/*.test.mjs, so raster-arithmetic-override.test.mjs must go. package.json:18 'measure' must go.
- 75 scripts/prepare-assets.mjs:17 pins face-a (keep the pin), but the script also writes public/models/manifest.json and public/mediapipe. It must never run against the read-only ../../ar/public.

Plan conflict to flag: PLAN WP1.3 rule 2 (whole-word lens/lenses/glass on material or node) would classify a 'lens holder' node as a lens. The existing classifier (geometry-comparison-core.mjs:106-110), its test (:29) and its smoke (:69) deliberately treat 'lens holder', 'lens rim' and 'lens frame' as non-lens through a structural-word exclusion. Recommend adding that exclusion to rule 2.

Second plan risk: PLAN WP1.2's 'temples = geometry behind the lens at |x|>45 mm' would misclassify deep front connectors. part-visibility-probe's fixture has them at x=±49 mm, z to -62.5 mm. Keep that fixture as the regression for the new temple finder.

I listed every throw on the stash load path; these are the findings that matter for WP1.2. Nothing was modified. I wrote two read-only GLB metadata scripts into the scratchpad (glbinfo.py, glbbounds.py) to read the proof assets.

1. **Line numbers.** The plan's numbers are the 75/main numbering; main's rear-drop.ts is byte-identical to 75's. Mapped to the stash copy:
   - rear-drop: 103→106, 105→108, 144-145→153-154, 149→158, 151→160, 169→178, 194→203
   - continuity pin: 30-46 → 29-49 (throws at 31, 44, 47)

2. **Crystal Tom Ford r9 is predicted to fail at main:151 / stash:160, not at :194 / :203.** This is from reading the code; WP1.6 should confirm it by re-running.
   - Its extras use the legacy `part_role` ('frame', 'temple_left', 'lens_left', ...). main/75/stash read only `partRole` (main optical-material.ts:39-44; untracked part-visibility.ts:17).
   - So 'Crystal acetate' (transmission 1) counts as optical through the transmission rule (stash optical-material.ts:160).
   - lensRearZM therefore lands at the crystal temple tip, z=-0.1472, giving startZM=-0.1622, which is behind the default clip of -0.11 (external.ts:11).
   - Only a clip in [-0.2, -0.163] gets past :160. :203 would then probably still pass, because the embedded gold cores (z -0.0128..-0.1451, |x| 0.055-0.070) give a shaft, and the crystal temples are drawn unclipped as lens.
   - Lens-ID signal (1), legacy part_role starting with 'lens' ('lens_left'/'lens_right'), fixes r9 without the positional fallback, provided frame/temple_* part_roles map to frame.

3. **Which failures abort what.**
   - Every throw in TryOnRenderer.create/configure aborts model loading (main.ts:315 → closeSession).
   - Continuity failures are caught (renderer.ts:436) but silently disable the hair endpoint. This happens for every ?model= without &sha256 (continuity.ts:44/:147).
   - A stale sha256 is NOT caught: it aborts the whole load (renderer.ts:415 → continuity.ts:47).
   - Pose and render throws end the live session through the frame-pump onError (main.ts:301).

4. **Silent fallbacks that hide real errors.** None of these throws; all must become report flags.
   - temple-terminal-fit.ts:93 returns null when one arm has no terminal-band samples, i.e. a missing temple becomes a silent fixed cap. Also :55, :95, :102, :108-109.
   - renderer.ts:451 swallows a TempleHeadFit failure.

   - external.ts:46/47/49 silently null out-of-range clip, width, sha256 and lensenv.
   - temple-cheek-contact.ts and temple-contact-depth.ts contain no throws.

5. **No throw enforces §2 Origin or Orientation.** rear-drop:203 and continuity:111/:134 are only symptoms. validate_spec must check them directly: bbox, temples at -Z on both sides of X, origin at the bridge underside.

6. **§2 Transforms is enforced in four places.**
   - part-visibility.ts:72-73 checks local matrices up to and including the root. It fires first for profiled Studio GLBs, because renderer.ts:455 runs before :486.
   - lens-material.ts:230 (tolerance 1e-10), rear-drop.ts:153 and continuity.ts:78 (tolerance 1e-12).
   - Recommendation: one validate_spec check with a float tolerance of about 1e-6, reported once.

7. **Units.** A baked millimetre copy fails at stash rear-drop:160, and its clip is silently dropped (external.ts:46). Unit detection and rescaling, with a loud §2 Units FAIL, must run before rear-drop and continuity.

8. **Temple sides must come from the sign of x, never from names.** The two naming conventions disagree:
   - Studio GLBs put Temple_Left at -X (FT1119 x[-0.0710,-0.0558]; Prada temple .003 x[-0.0714,-0.0470]).
   - The ar_v4 r9 'Temple left' is at +X (x[+0.0531,+0.0718]).

9. **Proof GLBs.** FT1119 quality-001 and the Prada delivery carry consistent partRole and LENSES_part_visibility on every node (profiled path), no LENSES_lens_appearance, and no node transforms. They should clear the stash refusals.

10. **Limits and decoders.** No triangle or texture limits exist on the load path; the only budgets are the canonical effective-group ones (effective-optical-topology.ts:42-66). The "warn above 300k / 4096" and the Draco/meshopt/KTX2 decoders are new code; today both parses build a bare GLTFLoader (renderer.ts:417, continuity.ts:156).

current_rules: VERDICT: the stash runtime has exactly one lens decision function, and it does not follow the required order. Step 1 is partial: it reads partRole from Object3D userData only, never material extras and never legacy part_role. Step 2 (names) does not exist in src. Step 3 (transmission) is not a last resort: it decides every material that lacks a role, it is re-evaluated live on every call, and it never warns. Alpha is never a lens signal. Nothing is reported anywhere. There is no src 'frame-roles' module: the rules live in src/eyewear/optical-material.ts plus untracked src/eyewear/part-visibility.ts, and tests/frame-roles.test.ts pins them.

R1 role lookup. stash untracked src/eyewear/part-visibility.ts:10-17: inherited() starts at the Mesh's userData.partRole and walks up through every non-Mesh ancestor, stopping at the first other Mesh. That includes the model root (:11-14). partRoleOf = inherited(object,'partRole') (:17). Copy 75 has the same logic inline at src/eyewear/optical-material.ts:39-46. Material userData (where three's GLTFLoader puts material extras, GLTFLoader.js:3684) is never read. GLTFLoader merges node extras over mesh extras on a single-primitive Mesh (mesh extras at :3897, then node at :4368). On a multi-primitive node the node extras sit on the parent Group, so partRoleOf picks mesh extras first. Precedence therefore flips with the primitive count.

R2 role to owner. stash src/eyewear/optical-material.ts:20-21: FRAME_PART_ROLES={'frame','temple'}, LENS_PART_ROLE='lens'. At :85-89 the owner is decided in this order: (a) LENSES_part_visibility region if present (front->frame, temple_left/right, lens); (b) partRole==='lens' -> lens; (c) partRole frame/temple -> 'frame' if isAuthoredFrontFrame (:48-71, needs partRole 'frame', an identity transform chain and every vertex z >= -0.03 m) else 'temple'; (d) anything else -> 'unknown'. prototype_mechanics: Verdict: the prototype drives the real TryOnRenderer correctly. It does so by reaching into private renderer fields, and it ran against main's ar/, not 75ae133. Pipeline: run.mjs starts Vite on ar/ with configFile:false (glasses3d/plan/prototypes/ar_capture/run.mjs:19). A plugin serves page.js as a virtual module, '/__junction.html', '/__junction/config.json' and the case GLBs at '/__junction/models/<id>.glb' (run.mjs:18-28). Playwright headless Chromium blocks every non-origin request (run.mjs:35-37), calls window.junction.run() once (run.mjs:42), then pulls each base64 PNG back and writes report.json (run.mjs:43-49).

Pose construction (page.js:7-15) is a copy of the provider harness function (75 and stash qa/provider-comparison-ar.html:13-21). 1) It loads the 468 canonical-face positions in cm from /models/canonical-face.json (page.js:26). Those positions are verified against face_landmarker.task (stash src/render/face-surface.ts:9-13). 2) It builds the matrix compose(T=(0,0,-depth), R=Euler(pitch,yaw,roll,'YXZ'), S=1) with depth defaulting to 23 cm (page.js:8). The YXZ order matches poseAngles (stash src/render/pose-stabilizer.ts:62-66), so the requested angles are reported back exactly. 3) It projects with v=2*tan(31.5 deg), the 63 deg vertical FOV of stash src/render/projection.ts:3, and h=v*W/H: x=.5+X/(-Z*h), y=.5-Y/(-Z*v), z=(-Z/meanDepth-1)/h. I checked the algebra: FaceSurface.reconstruct (stash src/render/face-surface.ts:85-118) recovers exactly these camera-space points (meanScreenZ=0, totalScale=1/mean, distance_i=d_i). 4) It appends 10 'iris' points, five identical copies each of the 33/133 and 362/263 eye-corner midpoints (page.js:13). That reaches the 478 landmarks the protocol requires (stash src/face/protocol.ts:35). 5) It returns {matrix, landmarks, inferenceMs:0}.

Sign conventions: yaw>0 turns the nose toward image +x in the unmirrored frame. The asset's -X side (the wearer's right) is then near the camera. pitch>0 tips the nose down, so the camera sees from above: config 'above20' = pitch +20. Views in the configs: front, above20, below20 (-20), below30 (-30), yawL35 (-35), yawR35 (+35), yawR30below15 (+30/-15), yawL25above15 (-25/+15) (config-main.json:5-6). This is not the plan's set: yaw +/-30/+/-45 and pitch +/-20, with junction poses at yaw +/-30 x pitch +/-20.

Settling (page.js:50-60). Warm-up poses the front detection 51 times, t=0..5000 ms in 100 ms steps, and requires instance.fitting.ready (page.js:52-53). The fit only measures within |yaw|<=18 and |pitch|<=20 (stash src/render/eyewear-fit.ts:16) and locks after one measurement (eyewear-fit.ts:81). Its scale is clamp(faceWidth*ratio/frontWidthCm, .85, 1.15)*1.08 (eyewear-fit.ts:132-136), with frontWidthCm taken from the asset's geometry (stash src/render/renderer.ts:487-488). The case width_mm therefore has no rendering effect: catalog.ts:99-100 stores it only as assumedWidthMm, and no file in src/render reads it. Each view then runs 30 more poses at +100 ms to settle the contact-depth and head-fit filters (page.js:60). Renderer options are {sync:false, steady:null} (page.js:42): no GPU fence, no pose stabilizer.

Backgrounds (page.js:16-21) are flat canvases: skin #cba68d, dark #2b2522, and a 32 px checker of #b4a190/#ebe0d2. No face image is drawn, so the glasses sit on a flat colour while the invisible face surface and head shell still occlude by depth (stash src/render/renderer.ts:494-505).

Variant rendering (page.js:61-84): for each view x background x variant, edits go on a restore stack. swap() replaces mesh.material and keeps the original in userData.__orig; setp() saves and sets a property. The page then calls instance.render(null, {hair:false, shadows:true, guard:true}), or {hair:false, shadows:false, guard:false} for 'plain', reads back with instance.readback() and restores in finally. Variants: base, plain, lens_hidden, lens_only, lens_nospec, env_off, lens_alpha (MeshPhysical opacity .18), lens_alpha_nospec (MeshBasic .18), lens_mask (magenta MeshBasic, toneMapped:false), lens_mask_double, lens_xray (cyan, depthTest off, renderOrder 999), normals (MeshNormalMaterial on all eyewear), lens_normals, lens_tonemapped, frame_flat (textured frame -> map null, colour 0x2a1a10), wire_mask (green on meshes matching /eyewire/i), lens_front_only.

capture.junction_crop_method: Locate each junction from geometry and measure it from renders. 1) Geometry, once per GLB, in asset-local metres inside the page. Split the lenses by side using connected components, or by vertex x-sign when one component spans the bridge (a shield); never by name. The non-lens front is the faces with z > -30 mm (AUTHORED_FRAME_FRONT_MIN_Z_M, stash src/eyewear/optical-material.ts:43), or the 'front' region when part-visibility profiles exist. Trim 8% off each end of each lens's x-range and take 24 stations x_i. At each station, slice the TRIANGLES with the plane x=x_i; vertex bins skip sparse brows silently (junction_geom.py:14-17). Lens top (y_t, z_t) = max-y point of the lens slice. Brow bottom y_b = lowest frame-slice point with y > y_t-3 mm and |z-z_t| < 6 mm. overlap_mm = (y_t-y_b)*1000: positive means seated, negative means a gap. 'No frame above' marks rimless or nylor tops. These numbers go into report.geometry.lens_top_vs_brow and feed check_lens_seating later. Per side, the junction box is the AABB of the stations with frame above, padded by x +/-1.5 mm, y [y_t-4 mm, max(y_b,y_t)+5 mm], z [z_t-4 mm, z_t+4 mm]. 2) Poses: yaw +/-30 x pitch +/-20 (4 poses, YXZ, same detection() and settle as page.js). After posing, project the 8 box corners with projectAssetPoints, which uses assetMatrixWorld including the fit scale. The crop rect is their bbox plus 16 px per side, clamped to the frame, minimum 96x48, saved at native pixels with an optional 2x nearest upscale for Astra (scale recorded). Both sides are captured. near = the side with the larger projected box area; for yaw>0 that is asset -X. This replaces the hard-coded view-id side choice in band_metrics.py:13. 3) Renders at each pose: beauty on skin and dark (the pale eyewire line depends on background brightness), plus a part-id render at the same pose. Inside each crop, for each column in the projected lens-top span, find the topmost lens-ID pixel and walk up at most the projected 3 mm. The first non-lens class is contact (any frame ID), gap (background), or another part. Report contact_cols_pct, gap_cols_pct, median_gap_px, per-mesh visible pixels in the band (this generalises the name-based wire_metric.py:12 to any part ID with no names), and band_metrics' white% and edge count on the beauty crop for continuity with the old numbers. Antialiasing mixes colours at edges, so decode by nearest palette colour within a tolerance and mark the rest 'mixed'. Part-id temples are drawn without the clip shader (only a renderer-side override would keep it), so part-id renders are valid for the front and junction only, and the report says so.

capture.proposed_layout: Lives at glasses3d/arview/. package.json maps bin 'arview' to bin/arview.mjs; 'npm run capture' runs node qa/capture.mjs; Playwright Chromium is installed once with npx playwright install chromium. vite.config.ts: publicDir '../../ar/public' (read-only), cacheDir inside arview/node_modules/.vite, worker {format:'es'}, optimizeDeps.include ['three', 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js', 'three/addons/environments/RoomEnvironment.js', '@mediapipe/tasks-vision'] so a cold cache cannot reload the page mid-run. CLI: arview capture <glb> --poses default|junction|all --out <dir> [--backgrounds skin,dark,checker] [--depth-cm 23] [--size 1280x854] [--lensenv N] [--clip auto|<m>] [--no-portrait] [--mirror] [--live-probe] [--step-timeout-s 60]. Pose sets: default = front, yaw +/-30, yaw +/-45, pitch +/-20 (7) x skin x {beauty, part_id}, plus the portrait. junction = yaw +/-30 x pitch +/-20 (4) x {skin, dark} beauty plus part_id, full frames plus 2 side crops each. all = both, plus checker, plus the diagnostic variants (lens_hidden, lens_only, normals, lens_xray). Modules: qa/capture.mjs is the Node orchestrator. It parses args, runs the GLB preflight, starts Vite and Chromium, builds a deterministic step list, and drives the page ONE STEP PER page.evaluate with a per-step timeout. On a stall it kills Chromium, writes a partial report and exits non-zero within about 2 min. It streams PNGs through page.exposeBinding('arviewEmit'), which writes each file at once and returns its sha256, then assembles report.json (written to .tmp and renamed with retry, because Defender denies some renames). qa/capture/cli.mjs: pure argument parsing. qa/capture/poses.mjs: pose sets and naming conventions (pure; shared with the page). qa/capture/synthetic-face.mjs: the page.js:7-15 detection(), plus a node test that round-trips it through FaceSurface.reconstruct. qa/capture/glb-preflight.mjs: Node-side GLB/JSON read covering the section-2 rows, external URIs, compression extensions, triangle and texture counts, and the units guess from the bbox (a millimetre file is flagged, x0.001 is applied as a loud fallback, and the units row fails). Section-2 logic lives in src/spec/validate-spec.ts, kept in agreement with WP3's Python validate_spec by shared golden fixtures. src/eyewear/lens-classify.ts: the 3-step lens order with per-material {class, signal}, used by both the renderer and the report. qa/capture/junction.ts: triangle slicing, overlap_mm, junction boxes and crop projection (pure, tested on synthetic fixtures). qa/capture/id-palette.mjs: palette and AA-tolerant decode. qa/capture/live-rules.mjs: static would-fail-live rules from RULES_AUDIT section C, plus main's external.ts ranges (clip [-0.2,-0.03] with default -0.11, width [60,250], lensenv [0.3,4], loopback; external.ts:11-12, :43-49). Optional --live-probe loads the GLB once on main's unmodified ar/ (Vite root read-only, cacheDir redirected into arview) and records the actual refusal text. qa/capture/report.mjs: report assembly (pure, tested). qa/pages/capture.html with capture-page.ts exposes window.arview = {init(request) -> {classification, geometry, runtime, warnings}, step(spec) -> metadata (image emitted via the binding), portrait(pins) -> metadata, dispose()}. qa/pages/portrait.ts is the portrait port. qa/portrait-contract.mjs is ported with its test; qa/lighting.mjs holds the moved lighting functions. report.json: {schema:'arview.capture/1', created_at, tool:{arview_commit, runtime_base, node, chromium, gpu_renderer, samples, float_color}, input:{path, bytes, sha256, embedded}, request:{...}, spec:{format, units, origin, orientation, transforms, geometry, components (each {pass, evidence}), verdict} (THE acceptance), classification:{materials:[{name, class, signal, meshes}], lens_sides}, geometry:{bbox_mm, triangles, max_texture_px, lens_top_vs_brow:[{side, x_mm, lens_top_y_mm, brow_bottom_y_mm, overlap_mm}], temples:{left/right:{present, length_mm, opaque, max_abs_x_mm}}}, geometry_errors:[{code:'TEMPLE_MISSING'|'LENS_MISSING'|'ARMS_SAME_SIDE'..., evidence}] (never suppressed by a fallback), warnings:[{code, message}], fallbacks:[{code, detail}], live_site:{would_fail, reasons:[{code, rule, evidence, source}], probe:'static'|'main-runtime'}, runtime:{fitting:{scale, limited, ready}, continuity, temple_clip:{policy, cutoff_m}, guard, canonical_lenses, translucent_frame}, captures:[{file, sha256, bytes, kind:'pose'|'junction'|'portrait', pose:{id, yaw, pitch, roll, depth_cm, order:'YXZ'}, background, variant, crop|null, side, near, mirrored:false, camera:{view, projection, w, h}, asset_to_world, timing:{guarded, passes, safeFallback, shadowsApplied}, metrics, send_to_astra}], id_palette:[{rgb, mesh, class, side}], errors, blocked_external, implementation:{before, after, stable}, status:'captured'|'captured_with_warnings'|'infrastructure_failed'}. Exit codes: 0 = spec pass and captured; 3 = spec fail but captured (Astra is never blocked); 1 = infrastructure failure.
prototype_defects: Wrong runtime: run.mjs:7 serves C:/Users/Shay/PycharmProjects/lenses/ar, which is main and older than 75ae133. The pre-repoint constant was the same path (scratchpad repoint.py:33). So the 'seated + rimsplit renders cleanly' WP4 baseline and every ab2/ab3/ab4/main sheet came from main's renderer, not the 75ae133+stash runtime the owner judged on (no eyewear-reflection glare fix, no part-visibility). Re-baseline on arview before WP4 compares against it.

The prototype writes into ar/. run.mjs:19 uses createServer({root: AR}) with no cacheDir, so Vite's dependency cache lands in ar/node_modules/.vite. The portrait has the same issue: cacheDir is root/node_modules/.vite-portrait-preview (75 qa/portrait-preview.mjs:54). Both break 'arview never modifies ar/'. Vite and Playwright are also imported from ar/node_modules (run.mjs:8-9). With no optimizeDeps.include, a cold cache can make Vite discover three/addons after page load and reload the page mid-evaluate (a risk, not observed).

Memory and stalls: every PNG of every case is held as a base64 data URL in window.junctionImages until the run ends (page.js:98, run.mjs:43-47). config-main produces 3 cases x 8 views x 11 variants = 264 frames at 1280x854 in page memory, and a crash loses all of them. The whole run is one page.evaluate with a 10-minute timeout (run.mjs:36, :42), so a hang is silent for 10 min (violates the no-silent-stalls rule).

No GPU check: report.gpu is recorded (run.mjs:48) but never checked, so a SwiftShader or software fallback, missing EXT_color_buffer_float or samples=0 would pass silently. Console errors and pageerrors are collected (run.mjs:38-39) but never fail the run. The guard result is not checked either: timing.guarded and safeFallback are not asserted for the base render (the portrait does assert it at stash html:88).

Variants are unreliable on crystal frames. render() swaps translucent twins in and leaves them on the meshes (stash renderer.ts:765-769, :804), so 'normals' shows twins, not normals, on crystal parts. A twin is cloned at first render from whatever the original holds then (stash translucent-twin.ts:115), and refresh copies only shader hooks (:177-185). If lens_only or frame_flat is the first variant of a case, the cached twin permanently inherits visible=false or map=null; restore() resets only the original. env_off leaves crystal envMaps on. The r9 crystal Tom Ford is exactly this case.

Swapped MeshBasic and MeshNormal materials drop the temple clip, visibility and hair shader hooks (installed through onBeforeCompile on the originals), so 'normals' draws full-length, unclipped arms. With canonical lenses, a swapped lens material leaks into CanonicalLensLayers' opaque-input pass, because the layers hide by material.visible on their own proxies (stash lens-layers.ts:72-77, :110). The 'transmission=' recorded per lens (page.js:46) is always 0 for canonical lenses, because the layers zero it (lens-layers.ts:71).

Name coupling, against section 2's 'no fixed mesh count or names': wire_mask uses /eyewire/i (page.js:80, wire_metric.py:12). band_metrics hard-codes 'TomFordClearMesh_1', 'left'/'right'/'lens'/'pad' tokens and a split at mid +/-30 px (band_metrics.py:4-5, :15-16), and picks the side from view-id strings (band_metrics.py:13). seat_copy.py:30 picks the side by 'Left' in the node name; junction_geom.py takes node names as arguments. lensMats is a Set of mesh.material without flattening, so multi-material meshes break (page.js:47).

Boxes: the bbox covers the whole lens mesh, keyed by name and blind to occlusion (page.js:86-94). One fused lens mesh holding both lenses gives a single box across both. Frame meshes are never boxed, despite the comment at page.js:85. The report stores no camera matrices, asset matrix or per-render fit (page.js:97), so geometry cannot be reprojected afterwards. 75 qa/provider-comparison-ar.html:114-133 already records these.

Registration: a fixed templeClipLocalZM of -0.14 (page.js:38). Short arms then fail continuity ('An original posterior arm cross-section is missing', stash continuity.ts:134), and the failure (instance.continuityFailure) is never reported. The stash replaced this with qa/temple-cutoff.mjs. width_mm=141.91 in the configs has no rendering effect (catalog.ts:99-100; no reader in src/render). There is no lensenv, so mirror lenses render differently from the owner's try-on link (75 qa/provider-comparison-lighting.mjs:28-37). The catalog import (page.js:4) and config-main's 'live' eyewearId case rely on the dropped catalog code.

Viewpoint: depth 23 cm (page.js:7) puts the glasses about 16.5 cm from the camera (front offset 6.53 cm, catalog.ts:8). That is about 2-3x closer than live use, with exaggerated perspective (the outer lens edges are seen at about 23 deg even in 'front'). Keep it only for WP4 parity and record it. For live-like close-ups, use about 45 cm plus a QA maxRenderWidth of 2560.

Synthetic iris landmarks are five identical points at the eye-corner midpoint, i.e. zero radius (page.js:13). Today nothing reads indices 468 and above (only the 478-count check, stash protocol.ts:35), but any iris-based scale would silently break. Minor: there is no default for config.variants (page.js:54 throws if it is missing), case ids are not sanitised before going into URLs and filenames (run.mjs:17, page.js:36), and wire_metric.py:4 reads 'ab4/report.json' relative to the working directory.

junction_geom.py: brow bottom = minimum y over ALL brow vertices in a 0.8 mm bin (:16-19), so near the endpieces it reads the endpiece bottom. Empty bins are skipped silently (:17). The 'upper eyewire' filter is y>0 (:24), not 'y > lens centre' as the header claims. glbmesh.py ignores node transforms and the hierarchy without checking identity (:21-28). rim_split.py classifies caps by face normal |z|>0.5 (:30), which misclassifies strongly wrapped lenses.

It reads private renderer fields (:67, :75, :85), and its lighting depends on the provider-harness file being dropped. The 75 version (75 html:61) used the fixed -0.14 cutoff, which fails short-arm models.
